independent_seed_review.comment: CLM-R4-PSY-PSYCHOTHERAPY entails that preference selects the modality, so the discriminator is cited; downgraded because it is defeated by the identical single fact as SEED-PSY-T03-PSYCHOTHERAPY and is a strict subset of it, so the two should not appear in one option set.

shared_features_with_key: a first-line psychological treatment offered as the initial plan
a treatment that answers the access constraint in the scenario
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who spots the access constraint, solves it with the digital format, and does not notice that the patient's preference, not access, is what selects the modality.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Cognitive behavioural therapy is efficacious across formats including digital delivery, which makes the digital route the natural answer to an access constraint.

seeds.author_rejection_reason: Two severity tiers away from the scenario and identified in the r3 independent verification as a weak distractor at exactly this target; no medically trained candidate selects it for a working, non-psychotic patient.
candidate_visible_discriminators: a non-psychotic moderate episode
seeds.competitor_concept: An atypical antipsychotic as initial monotherapy
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct in combination with an antidepressant for a severe episode with psychotic symptoms.

independent_seed_review.comment: Checks 4 and 5 fail: CLM-R2-PSY-ANTIPSYCHOTIC restricts the agent to severe episodes with psychotic symptoms, two tiers from a working, non-psychotic outpatient, so no trained candidate selects it as initial monotherapy. Agrees with the author.

shared_features_with_key: a pharmacological initial treatment
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who recalls the placement without the conditions attached to it.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Atypical antipsychotics appear in the guideline's depression recommendations.

seeds.author_rejection_reason: Identified in the r3 independent verification as severity-mismatched by two tiers at this exact target; retained in the pack only to record that it was reconsidered and refused.
candidate_visible_discriminators: a moderate outpatient episode with low safety risk
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct in the most severe episodes and life-threatening situations.

independent_seed_review.comment: Checks 4 and 5 fail for the same reason: CLM-R2-PSY-ECT confines it to the most severe or life-threatening episodes, so it is severity-mismatched by two tiers in a moderate outpatient episode with low safety risk. Agrees with the author.

shared_features_with_key: a first-choice option named in the guideline
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who recalls first-choice without the severity condition.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Electroconvulsive therapy can be a first-choice option in the guideline.

targets.decision_context: An evaluation report comparing survival after diagnosis between screen-detected and clinically detected cases.
targets.lead_in_dimension: Which methodological explanation best accounts for the pattern in these results?
targets.learner_decision: Identify lead-time bias when screening advances diagnosis and lengthens measured postdiagnosis survival without changing age at death or disease-specific mortality.

candidate_visible_discriminators: an unchanged distribution of tumour grade or growth rate between the groups
an unchanged age at death, which points at the start of the clock rather than the mix of disease
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where the screened group contains a disproportionate share of slowly progressing variants of the disease.

independent_seed_review.comment: CLM-R2-PHELO-LENGTH entails that length bias operates through a disproportionate share of slow-progressing variants, so an unchanged disease mix defeats it; case-mix and age-at-death figures are ordinary content of the evaluation report described, not exclusion clauses.

shared_features_with_key: longer measured survival in screen-detected cases without a treatment effect
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who has learned the two biases as a pair and cannot separate them without deliberately checking whether the disease mix or the diagnosis date moved.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Length bias is the other classic screening bias that inflates apparent survival in screen-detected cases, and both act through the composition or timing of the screened group rather than through treatment.

candidate_visible_discriminators: equal numbers of cases diagnosed in the two groups
no excess incidence in the screened population
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where more cases are diagnosed in the screened group than in the unscreened group.

independent_seed_review.comment: CLM-R2-PHELO-OVERDIAGNOSIS entails the excess-incidence signature (up to 30 percent more cancers in the screened group), so equal case counts is a positive reported datum that defeats it.

shared_features_with_key: an apparent survival benefit produced by the act of screening rather than by treatment
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who knows overdiagnosis is the fashionable screening critique and reaches for it whenever survival improves without mortality falling.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Overdiagnosis inflates survival statistics by adding cases that would never have surfaced, and it is documented at up to thirty percent excess incidence in breast screening.

candidate_visible_discriminators: groups assembled by allocation rather than by choice, with comparable baseline health
a survival difference that is present in the timing of diagnosis rather than in the health of the people
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where the compared groups self-selected and differ in baseline health.

independent_seed_review.comment: CLM-R2-PHELO-HEALTHY-VOLUNTEER entails that the bias arises where groups self-select, so a stated allocation design with comparable baseline health is a positive study-design fact that decides it.

shared_features_with_key: a comparison that makes screening look better than it is
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who defaults to selection bias whenever screened and unscreened groups are compared.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: People who choose screening are healthier to begin with, so observational comparisons of attenders against non-attenders routinely favour screening for reasons unrelated to it.

candidate_visible_discriminators: an unchanged threshold across the compared periods
an unchanged number of people investigated
seeds.competitor_concept: A cut-off set too far toward the low-risk end
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where the threshold choice, rather than the timing of diagnosis, has changed who is called a case.

independent_seed_review.comment: Checks 2 and 6 fail: a cut-off placement is a programme design parameter, not a named methodological explanation for an apparent survival benefit, and CLM-R2-PHELO-CUTOFF speaks only to missed cases and investigation costs, entailing nothing about post-diagnosis survival comparisons. This is the same category defect the author himself rejected at SEED-PHELO-T02-THRESHOLD. Disagrees with the author's ACCEPTABLE.

shared_features_with_key: a screening design feature that changes the measured performance of the programme
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who explains any distortion in screening figures by the cut-off, which is the parameter most often taught as adjustable.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: A permissive threshold enlarges the detected case pool with milder disease, which is the mechanism a candidate reaches for when the screened group looks healthier.

candidate_visible_discriminators: a result driven by when the clock starts rather than by how often people are screened
seeds.competitor_concept: A screening interval mismatched to the disease's natural history
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where the interval is too long relative to the sojourn time and interval cancers dominate.

independent_seed_review.comment: Checks 2 and 6 fail: CLM-R4-PHELO-INTERVAL says only that the interval should follow natural history and test sensitivity and entails nothing about measured survival after diagnosis, and a screening interval is a programme parameter rather than a methodological bias. Disagrees with the author's ACCEPTABLE.

shared_features_with_key: a programme design feature offered to explain a survival pattern
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who has memorised the interval criterion and applies it to any screening result that looks anomalous.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: The interval must be set from the natural history of the disease and the sensitivity of the test, so an ill-chosen interval is a genuine explanation for a programme's measured performance.

targets.acquisition_note: The r3 item failed because two options were programme-design parameter changes rather than revisions to the invitation, leaving the key as the only option in the correct category. Every seed in this pack is an edit to the text of the same letter, and the two programme-parameter concepts that caused the r3 failure are carried as explicit rejections.
targets.decision_context: A drafted population screening invitation letter whose current wording is quoted in the stem.
targets.intended_key: Replace the relative benefit figure with the absolute chance of benefit and the chance of a false positive result
targets.lead_in_dimension: Which revision to the wording of the invitation letter would best protect the autonomy of the people invited?
targets.learner_decision: Require transparent informed consent and protection of autonomy before a population screening program exposes asymptomatic people to false positives and downstream procedures.

candidate_visible_discriminators: readers who perceive more authority than the recommendation carries may abdicate their right to informed consent
an edit that changes persuasion rather than information
seeds.competitor_concept: Add a line stating that the medical officer of health recommends that you attend
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where uptake, not autonomy, is the objective being optimised.

independent_seed_review.comment: An edit to the same letter at the same granularity, and CLM-R2-PHELO-REMINDERS entails the precise harm (perceived authority leading readers to abdicate informed consent) with CLM-R2-PHELO-ACCEPTABILITY supplying the obligation.

shared_features_with_key: an edit to the same invitation letter
an edit intended to change how the reader responds to the invitation
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who conflates a well-run programme with a persuasive one and does not know the guidance that authority framing erodes consent.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Adding an authoritative endorsement raises uptake, which is the programme's stated objective, and it is the edit a public health team would naturally propose.

candidate_visible_discriminators: an edit that adds no information about benefit or harm
the same authority effect that lets a reminder be read as an instruction
seeds.competitor_concept: Add a line saying that a reminder will be sent if you do not attend
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where the aim is to improve uptake in a programme whose information content is already adequate.

independent_seed_review.comment: CLM-R2-PHELO-REMINDERS entails both the uptake benefit that makes it attractive and the autonomy harm that defeats it against an autonomy-framed lead-in.

shared_features_with_key: an edit to the same invitation letter
an evidence-based change to the invitation process
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who recognises the evidence for reminders and selects the option that is supported by evidence rather than the one that answers the autonomy question asked.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Reminders demonstrably improve screening uptake, so telling the reader one is coming is an evidence-based edit with a real effect.

candidate_visible_discriminators: a count without a denominator, which does not give an individual reader a chance of benefit
a benefit figure added while the harms remain undisclosed
seeds.competitor_concept: Add the number of cancers the programme detected last year
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where the reader also has the denominator and the harms, so the figure can be interpreted.

independent_seed_review.comment: CLM-R4-PHELO-ABSOLUTE entails that an individual reader needs an absolute personal figure rather than an impressive aggregate, and CLM-R4-PHELO-FALSEPOS entails the harm that an autonomy-protecting letter must also disclose.

shared_features_with_key: an edit that adds numerical information to the letter
an edit presented as improving transparency
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who equates disclosing a number with informed consent and does not ask whether the number tells the reader anything about their own risk.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Adding a concrete figure looks like exactly the transparency the question is asking for, and it is the edit most likely to be proposed by someone who has been told to add numbers.

candidate_visible_discriminators: results that must be clearly interpretable to the person receiving them
figures that do not tell an individual reader their chance of a false positive
seeds.competitor_concept: Add the sensitivity and specificity of the screening test
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct as programme documentation, where the audience can interpret the figures.

independent_seed_review.comment: CLM-R4-PHELO-ABSOLUTE entails that figures which do not translate to an individual's own chance fail the purpose; CLM-R4-PHELO-ACTION-POLICY is about programme test characteristics rather than letter content, so the entailment is partial and the seed is ACCEPTABLE rather than STRONG.

shared_features_with_key: an edit that adds performance information to the same letter
an edit framed as disclosure
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who treats completeness of technical information as equivalent to informed choice.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Test performance is a real programme criterion and quoting it appears to be full disclosure, which makes it attractive to a candidate who thinks more technical detail equals more consent.

seeds.author_rejection_reason: Named in the r3 independent verification as the exact defect at this target: it is a programme eligibility or cut-off decision rather than a revision to the invitation, so it answers a different lead-in dimension and is discarded by any candidate who reads the question.
candidate_visible_discriminators: it says nothing about how the invitation informs the reader
seeds.competitor_concept: Lower the threshold at which a result is called abnormal
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct as a programme design question, not as a revision to an invitation.

independent_seed_review.comment: Checks 1, 2 and 4 fail: lowering the abnormal-result threshold is a programme parameter change, not a revision to the invitation text, so it answers a different lead-in dimension and is discarded by anyone who reads the question. Agrees with the author.

shared_features_with_key: a change to the screening programme
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who does not read the lead-in.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Threshold choice is a real programme decision.

targets.decision_context: A screening programme whose confirmatory and treatment capacity is quantified and falls short of the expected volume of positive results.
targets.intended_key: Defer the launch until diagnostic and treatment capacity is in place
targets.lead_in_dimension: What should the programme do about the planned launch?
targets.learner_decision: Defer population screening until a coordinated pathway can confirm positive results and deliver effective early treatment.

candidate_visible_discriminators: a confirmatory bottleneck that a smaller volume does not remove
people invited in the pilot district who still cannot be confirmed or treated
seeds.competitor_concept: Launch in a single district as a pilot and expand later
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where the constraint is cost or logistics rather than an absolute shortfall in the confirmatory pathway.

independent_seed_review.comment: A complete programme decision matching the key's granularity, and CLM-R4-PHELO-HARM-LABEL plus CLM-R2-PHELO-FACILITIES entail that labelling anyone without confirmatory capacity is the harm, which a smaller catchment does not cure.

shared_features_with_key: a decision about whether and how to start the programme
a plan that takes the capacity constraint seriously
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who reaches for staged rollout as the generic answer to any capacity constraint without asking whether the bottleneck scales down with the volume.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Staged implementation is standard programme practice, it manages cost, and screening is required to be a continuing process rather than a one-off project.

candidate_visible_discriminators: a threshold set too far toward the high-risk end will miss patients who could have benefitted
a shortfall so large that closing it by threshold would forfeit the programme's purpose
seeds.competitor_concept: Raise the threshold so that fewer results are called positive
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where the current threshold sits too far toward the low-risk end and is generating avoidable low-yield referrals.

independent_seed_review.comment: CLM-R2-PHELO-CUTOFF entails the cost on the other side of the trade-off, that a threshold set too far toward the high-risk end misses patients who could have benefitted, so the arithmetic fix is defeated on cited grounds.

shared_features_with_key: a programme decision that changes how many people enter the confirmatory pathway
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who solves the capacity arithmetic and does not price the missed cases on the other side of the trade-off.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Moving the cut-off is the one lever that directly matches referral volume to available capacity, and the guidance itself frames the cut-off as a two-sided trade-off.

candidate_visible_discriminators: evaluation that measures harm after it has occurred rather than preventing it
asymptomatic people labelled as possibly diseased while confirmation is unavailable
seeds.competitor_concept: Launch as planned with continuing evaluation against programme goals
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct as a standing requirement of any programme that does launch.

independent_seed_review.comment: CLM-R4-PHELO-EVALUATION makes it a genuine obligation and CLM-R4-PHELO-HARM-LABEL entails that evaluation records harm after it occurs rather than preventing the labelling harm the stem describes.

shared_features_with_key: a complete programme decision about the launch
a course of action grounded in a named programme criterion
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who selects the option carrying a recognised programme criterion without asking whether the criterion addresses the specific shortfall described.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Continuing evaluation against clear goals is an explicit criterion for a screening programme, so proposing it is proposing a genuine obligation.

candidate_visible_discriminators: a shortfall that is one of capacity rather than of cost-effectiveness
a study that does not create confirmatory or treatment capacity
seeds.competitor_concept: Commission an economic evaluation before deciding
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where the open question is whether the programme represents value for money.

independent_seed_review.comment: CLM-R4-PHELO-ECONOMIC makes commissioning a study defensible governance and CLM-R2-PHELO-FACILITIES entails that the described shortfall is one of capacity, which a study does not create; ACCEPTABLE because it is the least tempting of the four.

shared_features_with_key: a decision to hold the launch pending further work
a course of action grounded in a named programme criterion
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who answers a resource-shaped problem with an economic study rather than reading which resource is missing.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: An economic evaluation of the programme is an explicit requirement, and the cost of screening a whole population is stated to be considerable, so commissioning one is defensible governance.

seeds.author_rejection_reason: Self-defeating against a stem that quantifies a confirmatory shortfall: increasing demand against a stated bottleneck is discarded without any public health knowledge, which is the weak-distractor pattern the calibrated rubric rejects.
candidate_visible_discriminators: a campaign that worsens the exact bottleneck described
seeds.competitor_concept: Launch with a public awareness campaign to maximise uptake
seeds.conditions_under_which_competitor_would_: Correct where capacity exceeds demand.

independent_seed_review.comment: Check 4 fails: increasing demand against a quantified confirmatory bottleneck is self-defeating on the face of the stem and is discarded without any public health knowledge. Agrees with the author.

shared_features_with_key: a decision about how to launch
seeds.why_a_partially_knowledgeable_candidate_: A candidate who does not read the capacity figures.
seeds.why_plausible_for_this_decision: Promotion raises uptake, which is a programme objective.
